14371295_7de25a1f.text: GABAergic inhibitory interneurons control fundamental aspects of neuronal network function
14371295_7de25a1f.section: Classical Functional and Morphological Interneuron Types

14371295_f5d269ca.text: We identified five interneuron classes, each of them characterized by a distinct set of anatomical and physiological parameters
14371295_f5d269ca.section: Classical Functional and Morphological Interneuron Types

14371295_8543c642.text: GABAergic cells fell into four morphological classes but diverged into three physiological classes with strong overlap among BC- and HIPP-like neurons in class P1 and between TML-, ML-, and HIPP-like cells in class P3
14371295_8543c642.section: Classical Functional and Morphological Interneuron Types

14371295_eba9a341.text: ML cells formed an exception; they could be classified on the basis of only their electrophysiological characteristics. TML cells could be largely but not entirely classified on the basis of electrophysiological parameters
14371295_eba9a341.section: Classical Functional and Morphological Interneuron Types

14371295_49ee101e.text: a combination of morphological and physiological characteristics resulted in the emergence of five classes with strong correlations between morphologically defined interneuron types and physiological properties
